gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured tracking force for the candidates. HIFI.DE measured 2.1 g on the Audio-Technica AT-LP70XBT and 3.7 g on the Sony PS-LX3BT, so the Sony presses the stylus into the groove about 76% harder.
standout_why: TurntableVerse (#1/#2, updated 2026-11-03) gives only Audio-Technica's and Pro-Ject's own wow-and-flutter and S/N specs. It says it did not test the decks and has no measured figures for speed, latency or tracking force. I could not read the text of the cited What Hi-Fi Bluetooth roundup, Louder's best-record-players page, TechRadar's PS-LX310BT review or the What Hi-Fi PS-LX3BT review: each fetch returned only the headline. VinylPickup failed with an SSL certificate error. So I can't rule out that those pages mention a tracking-force spec. Nothing I could read side by side has measured figures.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's pick of the AT-LP70XBT over the Sony PS-LX3BT, which costs $50 more. Measured on the same site by the same reviewer, the AT tracks at 2.1 g and the Sony at 3.7 g. A lighter stylus wears records less, and HIFI.DE also found the AT runs at a fairly steady speed with barely audible motor noise. HIFI.DE's scores lean the same way, narrowly: 7.5 for the AT and 7.4 for the Sony. For the JBL Spinner BT, LB Tech Reviews measured 0.75% wow and flutter, enough that a held piano note audibly wavers. That is a reason to rank it below the AT and Sony automatics, despite its aptX HD.

findings.label: Measured tracking force (HIFI.DE)
findings.source_title: Audio-Technica AT-LP70XBT im Test: Richtig guter Plug-and-Player (HIFI.DE)
findings.note: Bernhard Rietschel, HIFI.DE, published 2025-06-27. Quote: 'stimmt beim Testgerät aufs Zehntel genau: 2,1 Gramm', i.e. accurate to a tenth of a gram on the test unit, mid-range for the VM95 series. No measuring tool named. The same review describes speed stability only in words ('läuft recht drehzahlstabil und mit kaum wahrnehmbarem Motorgeräusch') and gives no rpm or wow-and-flutter number. Score 7.5/10.

findings.label: Measured tracking force (HIFI.DE)
findings.source_title: Sony PS-LX3BT im Test: Vollautomat bekommt stylisches Upgrade (HIFI.DE)
findings.note: Bernhard Rietschel, HIFI.DE, published 2026-07-30, after four weeks of testing. Quote: 'Bei unserem Sony PS-LX3BT messen wir 3,7 Gramm, was noch im von AT empfohlenen Bereich liegt' (we measure 3.7 g, still within the range AT recommends for the cartridge). Arithmetic: 3.7 / 2.1 = 1.76, about 76% more downforce than the AT-LP70XBT measured by the same reviewer. No tool named. Score 7.4/10.

findings.label: Measured speed at 33⅓ rpm (LB Tech Reviews)
findings.source_title: Review: JBL Spinner BT (L&B Tech Reviews)
findings.note: Lasse Svendsen, published 2023-12-18. Reviewer called the deviation within the acceptable range. No 45 rpm figure and no measuring tool or method stated.

findings.label: Measured wow and flutter (LB Tech Reviews)
findings.source_title: Review: JBL Spinner BT (L&B Tech Reviews)
findings.note: Lasse Svendsen, 2023-12-18. Quote: 'the measurements showed a deviation of 0.75 per cent. In practice, this means that you can hear a piano note fluctuate in pitch.' Weighting standard not stated. For comparison, TurntableVerse (read 2026-11-10) lists Audio-Technica's spec for the AT-LP70XBT as <0.25%, but that is a maker spec, not a measurement.

unsourced: Measured speed, wow and flutter, or Bluetooth latency for the AT-LP70XBT, PS-LX3BT, AT-LP60XBT and PS-LX310BT. Searched for lab or bench figures from Hi-Fi News, LB Tech Reviews, AnalogPlanet (403) and HIFI.DE (tracking force only). Search results showed only maker specs.
